title: About 1,700 buildings stand today in the path of Robert Moses's unbuilt expressways
description: Whose utopia? Robert Moses drew one man's perfect city of expressways through other people's neighborhoods. Many were built, like the Cross Bronx and the BQE. Four never were: the Lower Manhattan, Mid-Manhattan, Bushwick and Cross-Brooklyn expressways. This map traces those routes through today's city, as wide as each plan's right-of-way, and counts the buildings and people now standing in their path.
